hops.name: Analysis tab, page 1: Select the portfolio (Client card or Prospect card)
hops.finding: The tab opens on page 1 with two cards. The Client card is enabled only when the header holds an accepted client (AnalysisTab.tsx:316); the Prospect card is always enabled. Pressing a card sets the page to the client composer (2) or the prospect upload ('prospect'). For Andrew (an Opal-internal principal) the choice is his own at the sitting; this read traces both branches and marks a row on_path YES when it sits on either.

hops.name: The composer and the portfolio basis: the Prospect upload branch, and the picked-client branch
hops.finding: UPLOAD branch: for an internal principal the card shows a firm select and sends the CARD's firm as selected_tenant; with no firm chosen it sends nothing and says so in words (stagedProspect.ts:159-162, ProspectComposer.tsx:268, 312, 434, 578). Andrew must name Cottonwood there. PICKED-CLIENT branch: the composer takes the header's client and accounts; it refuses to read the catalogue or submit with no firm tenant (GenerateComposer.tsx:165-197), the tenant coming from selectedTenantFor (index.tsx:153-164); but its snapshot id is the browser-built source_set_revision join (GenerateComposer.tsx:209-211, adapt.ts:1121), not the server's cst_ id, so this branch cannot submit (row S13).

hops.name: The request the browser sends
hops.finding: Upload: POST /analysis/inputs with the file base64 and ?selected_tenant=<firm> (investor-reporting.ts:1100-1103). Generate: POST /analysis with {request_id, input_id, client_id null, account_ids [], snapshot_id null, variant, comparison_keys, report_title, prepared_for} and ?selected_tenant=<firm> (prospect.ts:139-155, stagedProspect.ts:171-174, investor-reporting.ts:1325-1336). No producer flag is sent; nothing the browser sends selects the producer (C-SWITCH).

hops.name: The route and its authorizer (the verified edge headers, then the firm binding)
hops.finding: POST /api/scoped/investor-reporting/analysis is served by irpt-ycharts-generate (entry.py:147-152, routes.json:71-79). Entry.handle requires the verified firm header (served.py:1177-1180); Andrew is an internal subject (x-firm-id opal-capital, served.py:307-319), so a selected_tenant different from the verified firm is admitted if it is in the registry and in his profile row's allowed list (served.py:1207-1230). Without selected_tenant the firm stays opal-capital, which is unmapped (row S12's origin). With Cottonwood chosen the request runs bound to the cottonwood tenant.

hops.name: Owner resolution for an internal principal (who owns the request)
hops.finding: For an internal subject the owner is built from his own identity at the input's firm: firm_id cottonwood, principal_id andrew@opalinvest.com, principal_class OPAL_GLOBAL (interactive_access.py:78-137, prospect_submission.py:72-73). An on-behalf advisor must be named only if the tenant is in the filer's allowedFirmIds (served.py:1056-1066); whether Andrew's own profile row lists cottonwood is a live data read this read did not make.

hops.name: Acceptance: frozen composition, retained input, atomic accept, queue send
hops.finding: submit_analysis validates the closed public body (submission.py:47-90), then SubmissionService.submit resolves the owner, re-authorizes, freezes the composition as a retained REQUEST_COMPOSITION, accepts it with acting_principal_id, then dispatches one queue message and answers {identity, stage RECEIVED} (submission_service.py:103-167). A failed send leaves the accepted record for recovery (dispatch_pending).

hops.name: The resident worker polls the queue and re-checks the acting principal
hops.finding: poll_once receives one message at 900 s visibility, execute() rebuilds the closed message from the accepted record and re-grades the owner's current profile row (current_authority.decide: active, home firm, created before acceptance, allowedFirmIds), so an OPAL_GLOBAL Andrew is allowed for cottonwood unless his row lists other firms. The message is deleted only on READY or ATTENTION (resident_worker.py:858-859); any exception leaves it to redeliver, five receives, then the dead-letter queue, with no record written for the generate kind (rows S49, S45).

hops.name: The resident worker's choice of producer (producer_for, the allow list)
hops.finding: producer_for reads the accepted record's owner.principal_id against OPAL_PRODUCER_PRINCIPALS = ('andrew@opalinvest.com',) (resident_worker.py:121-133). Andrew's owner principal_id is his sign-in (hop 5), so his job is OPAL; any other principal takes the YCharts path. The Opal stores are built only for a listed principal (resident_installed.py:239-251), including the firm's research-principal S3 client, which assumes irpt-<firm>-ycharts-research-role (runner.py:479-493): present for cottonwood, absent for other firms per row D2-S19 (not re-read live).

hops.name: The Opal producer: read holdings, classify, compute, render, record
hops.finding: produce() reads the frozen holdings from the firm store, reads classifications from the one table, computes the three classified elements and marks every price-based, builder-only and vendor-call element NOT_IN_THIS_VERSION (C-V1), renders the Opal-branded PDF with no vendor wording (layout_overview.py:961-962, 1053-1054; Data: Opal Capital), builds run.json and the AnalysisReport v2 document (opal_producer.py:272-339). No vendor call is made. inputs_as_of carries the date the run read each input, not each input's own date (row W1-S10).

hops.name: Retention and publish: PDF artifact, document spill, checkpoint, READY
hops.finding: run_opal retains the PDF as a YCHARTS_OPAL_REPORT artifact, checkpoints it, retains the whole Opal document as a json artifact on every Opal checkpoint (publication_worker.py:96-99; row W3-S13), publishes through the publisher's Opal branch, marks READY and sends I3 (resident_worker.py:449-490). run.json's report.key names the layout's own S3 address although the PDF went to the artifact (opal_producer.py:305-313; row W3-S16).

hops.name: The status read and the sections read
hops.finding: GET /status/{jobId} (irpt-status) maps the durable phase to a public state; READY becomes READY only when the date opt-in header is sent and the retained input's dates derive (owned_status.py:43-58, prospect_dates.py:30-65 now has an OPAL_ENGINE branch). GET /analysis/{jobId}/sections answers provider, request_ref, sections, computation_validation, retained_ref for an Opal document (owned_report.py:96-100). The published response schema still requires extraction_validation and forbids those members (analysis-report.response.schema.json:48-52; rows W2-S13, W6-S4): the answer is served outside the published contract.

hops.name: The page that opens the report: Your analysis requests, the opened request, Report sections
hops.finding: After Generate the report is opened from OwnedRequestHistory, a dialog that reads the request, then the sections (OwnedRequestHistory.tsx:326-339) and shows RetainedSections (:407). That list is mounted only when the header holds a client (AnalysisTab.tsx:397). RetainedSections calls SectionBlock without the Opal flag and reads a slice that carries no provider (adapt.ts:1412-1419), so an Opal report prints 'Vendor attribution:' per section and 'Extraction validation' under Technical details (OwnedRequestHistory.tsx:155-165, NativeSections.tsx:105-190). The Opal-aware NativeSections is rendered only by RequestList (a list the live client does not serve). The Prospect composer's own inline status mounts without selected_tenant (ProspectComposer.tsx:584). Filed as rows D2-W14-S1 and D2-W14-S2.
